title: The Holy Family
hookLine: the Sunday after Christmas honors an ordinary family life

cards: Between the infant in the manger and the grown man at the Jordan, Luke gives one scene. Jesus is twelve.
The family goes up to Jerusalem for Passover with a crowd of relatives, and on the way home, a full day's walk out, Mary and Joseph realize he isn't with the cousins. Three days of searching follow.
On the Sunday after Christmas, the Church sets aside the angels and the star and looks at a family: worried, tired, and very ordinary.

teach.b: They find him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions. Mary says: your father and I have been searching for you, sorrowing.
He answers that they should have known he must be about his Father's business. Luke says they didn't understand. Then the sentence the whole feast leans on.

teach.h: HE WENT DOWN, AND WAS SUBJECT.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them." The one John called the Word that made all things goes home and does what his parents tell him.

teach.h: THE QUIET YEARS IN ONE LINE.
teach.b: Then Luke folds every year until he is about thirty into one line: "And Jesus advanced in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men." That's almost everything we know.
Mark's gospel calls him the carpenter, using a Greek word for a builder or craftsman. The Gospels are silent about the rest: no stories of his teenage years, his friends, the day Joseph died.

Tradition fills the silence with what Catholics call the hidden life, the long years at Nazareth of work, meals, prayer and village life. Today's calendar keeps the feast on the Sunday after Christmas.

The point isn't that this family was perfect. Luke shows them anxious, confused, misunderstanding each other. The point is that most of the years Luke counts were spent at Nazareth, among relatives, at ordinary work.
Catholics see in that a dignity for every family's daily life, the dishes included.

how: Catholics keep the feast of the Holy Family on the Sunday within the octave of Christmas (or on December 30 when there is no such Sunday), and some parishes bless families or renew marriage vows that day.

games.q: you're twelve. your parents have searched three days and find you in the temple. your mother says, we've been searching for you, sorrowing. what do you say?
o: sorry, I lost track of time.
didn't you know I must be about my Father's business?
I was going to walk home tomorrow.
games.why: he answers that they should have known he'd be about his Father's business. then he goes home with them and is subject to them.

practice: Choose one family chore you usually sigh at, the dishes, the laundry, a call to a relative you owe, and picture doing it slowly and gladly, maybe without being asked, with the faces of the people you share a life with in mind.
Families come in many shapes; yours counts. If you pray, offer the chore for them; if not, simply hold them in mind.

wordCard.voice: Tekton, a builder. Mark's gospel word for Jesus, usually rendered carpenter, from the long hidden years of ordinary work at Nazareth. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: a builder or craftsman, Mark 6:3's word for Jesus, usually rendered carpenter.

carryVoice: Your line: an ordinary family. Most of his years looked like this. That's six hundred forty-three days.
